questions.q: What is the biggest mistake this lesson identifies when presenting a dashboard to a time-pressed stakeholder?
options: Offering to follow up on a question outside the report's scope
Opening with a one-sentence answer to the stakeholder's actual question
Walking through every visual top to bottom, narrating what each one is before saying what it means
Using the slicer live during the conversation
questions.explain: A visual-by-visual tour is backwards for someone in a hurry — the lesson recommends leading with the answer instead.

questions.q: What should the first 10-15 seconds of the walkthrough consist of?
options: The headline, stated as a sentence answering the stakeholder's actual question, drawn from the KPI cards
A tour of the Power Query transformation steps
A full explanation of how the T-SQL query was written
The detail table, opened before anything else
questions.explain: The structure is headline first, then the 'why' (the bar chart), then detail only if asked — not a tour starting from technical build steps.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend clicking the Territory slicer live during the conversation rather than just describing it?
options: Live demonstration is required for all Power BI presentations by Microsoft's guidelines
The slicer cannot be demonstrated any other way in the Power BI Service
Watching the report actually respond is more convincing to the stakeholder than being told it can filter
Describing the slicer verbally would take longer than clicking it
questions.explain: A live demonstration lets the stakeholder see the KPI cards and chart update in real time, which lands better than a verbal description.

questions.q: How should you respond if the stakeholder asks for a year-over-year comparison that this report was never scoped to include?
options: Explain that Power BI technically cannot support year-over-year comparisons
Guess at an approximate year-over-year number to avoid seeming unprepared
Apologize at length and avoid answering the question directly
Give a short, honest answer that it's out of scope for this version and offer to add it as a follow-up
questions.explain: A brief, honest scoping response protects credibility and turns the gap into the start of a next iteration, rather than undermining the report.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when should the detail table be opened during the presentation?
options: Only if the stakeholder asks a follow-up question that specifically needs it, not narrated by default
Always, immediately after the KPI cards, regardless of the conversation
Only after the report has been republished to a new workspace
Before the headline is stated, to establish full context first
questions.explain: The table is the 'detail, on request' step — it's shown only when a specific follow-up calls for it, keeping the walkthrough headline-first.
